thread.title: Apple: Prepare For An Entry - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Sandeep Singh Ahluwalia
title: Apple: Prepare For An Entry - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
From the beginning of November 2018, Apple’s ( AAPL ) share price has been in decline which has resulted in the stock tumbling by roughly 24%. This fall was triggered when news was released that Apple’s growth engine, the iPhone, has had a drop in its sales volume. However, I do not believe this is enough of a reason for investors to dump this stock. I say that as I believe Apple is a company with much more to offer than the iPhone. Thus, in this article, I shall ascertain the possibility of Apple having a slight fall after which it shall commence a strong bullish ascent. Hence, to establish the likelihood of this occurring, I will look at the fundamentals of the stock while also analyzing the charts using technical analysis tools.
Fundamental facets that matter: Apple’s big fat wallet:
One of the biggest benefits Apple has is its enormous stockpile of cash. This is as its cash level in 2018 stood at a whopping $256.8 billion . Thus, Apple can use some of its deep pockets to buy up businesses which can help improve the firm’s growth while also diversifying its portfolio. On the other hand, Apple can increase its spending on research and development activities which will allow the firm to design innovative new products that can unlock future growth scenarios. Moreover, the deep pockets also mean that Apple will continue buying back more shares which will make investors a very happy bunch. This in turn will cause a rise in its share price.
Apple’s Dividend level:
There was a time when Apple couldn’t be classified as a dividend stock. However, things have now changed as Apple currently pays the highest dividend in the world. I say that as Apple increased its dividend rate by 10.5% to $13.22 billion annually, which is higher than Exxon Mobil’s (NYSE: XOM ) dividend payout level of $12.77 billion. Thus, this is one of the reasons I am bullish on Apple in the long term. This is the fifth annual dividend hike since 2012 when Apple paid out its first dividend. Moreover, I do not see this trend changing, as this is a luxury made possible by the tech giant’s large cash pile. Thus, I expect dividend levels to rise consistently which will make Apple a favorite amongst long-term investors who are searching the market for well-paying dividend stocks. This is a very important factor for the firm as it ensures that money will keep flowing into the stock, which will cause the share price to appreciate as the level of selling from this group of investors is extremely low.
App store:
Apple’s applications are some of the best consumer products made. Thus, this results in the brand enjoying a high level of loyalty from its clientele. I say that as most people who utilize Apple devices will continue to use them, which will help grow Apple's ecosystem. Moreover, a proof of this trend is seen in 2017’s App Store statistics. This is as the number of App Store downloads in 2017 reached a whopping 180 billion . Hence, this coupled with the high sales volume of Apple devices will ensure that this segment grows exponentially. Moreover, Apple recently reported that it shipped out its 2 billionth iOS device, which reinforces the fact that the growth potential of the App Store is extremely high.
Data Privacy:
Apple has always been a pioneer in data privacy, which is what has ensured that its clientele feel more secure about the products. I chose to highlight this as I believe it will boost the firm’s growth in the future. I say that as consumers are becoming increasingly aware of privacy related issues. Therefore, Apple making an acquisition related to privacy protections will most definitely elevate its standing in the market. This is as Apple this year purchased Silk Labs, which is a platform that incorporates privacy by design as it only sends tiny portions of anonymized data to train its Artificial Intelligence algorithms. However, the key fact to note here is that Silk Labs ensures that its Artificial Intelligence software performs most of the functions on the client's device. This results in majority of the processing being done locally. Hence, this eliminates the need of sending data to Apple which in turn boosts the privacy of the client, as it provides the user with more control over their information. Therefore, I expect the Silk Labs deal to strengthen the firm's AI software and data privacy while also boosting the popularity of Apple’s gadgets and services as consumers will feel safer using them.
Apple’s financials are positive:
In my opinion, Wall Street simply freaked out over Apple’s earnings. I say this as when we look at the negative effect on the share price, one may believe that Apple’s earnings were extremely bad. However, that is far from the truth as the financial results were excellent. I say that as the revenue level grew by 19.6% to $62.9 billion, which is the fastest growth rate seen in the prior three years. Moreover, the earnings per share came in at $2.91, which surpassed analyst estimates by $0.13. This growth was primarily driven by two factors. The first factor was the 29% increase seen in iPhone’s revenue, which was a result of Apple raising the average sales price from $618 in the third quarter of 2017 to $793 in the fourth quarter of 2018. The second factor was the Apple Watch and Home Pod speaker. This is as these two products have had a high level of growth which has resulted in them accounting for 23% of the firm’s sales. This supports my notion that Apple’s future is bright as it is successfully diversifying its business from being over reliant on the iPhone.
Licensing:
I expect licensing payments to boost Apple’s financials down the road. I say that as Apple already receives a sizable amount of licensing fees from various third parties. However, the bulk of these payments come from Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) which pays Apple so that it can be the default search engine for the Safari browser and Siri. Moreover, the current payment from Google alone stands at a whopping $9 billion in 2018. Thus, this alone accounts for nearly 25% of Apple’s services segment revenues in 2018 and it is extremely probable that this is pure profit as there are no direct expenses involved. Hence, this clearly shows that down the road the value attained from this segment will rise as Apple’s product sales might have slowed down on a year-over-year basis but are still growing strongly.
Subscriptions:
Source: Loup Ventures
Subscriptions are one factor that I believe will be a growth driver for Apple in the future. I say that as Apple’s own subscriptions have grown significantly. A good example of this is Apple Music which has reached a whopping 56 million subscribers as of November 2018. Thus, I believe this trend will continue as Apple gadget users will take up more of the services to get a better overall experience. Apple has been converting customers from free to paid subscribers 2.5 times faster than its key rival Spotify (NYSE: SPOT ). Over the past year, Apple Music has had a conversation rate of 0.64%, against Spotify’s conversion rate of 0.24%.
On the other hand, I expect Apple to see growth in its commissions from subscriptions. I chose to highlight this as Apple charges a recurring commission of approximately 15% from all subscriptions made on its devices. Moreover, these commissions brought in $330 million in October alone, which is a 50% growth on a year-on-year basis. Hence, this clearly shows that there is a high level of potential to be banked upon here. This in turn will help Apple grow its profits and share price down the road.
Technical analysis: Price History:
As mentioned earlier, the share price of Apple has been in free fall of late. Thus, the big question is whether the charts had shown signs of a downfall. The answer to this is yes. There were several technical indicators pointing out that Apple’s share price will be falling steeply.
The first sign of a share price drop was given to us by the moving averages. On 24 th October, the share price fell below the 50-day moving average. This was then made worse when the 20-day moving average crossed below the 50-day moving average in the next two to three sessions. This clearly indicated to investors that there was trouble around the corner. Moreover, investors were then provided a further hint due to the formation of a large falling window. This pattern psychology echoes to investors how strongly one sided the market is in favor of the bears. Additionally, at this point, the share price had also fallen below the Ichimoku cloud, which signaled that the bearish strength is extremely high. However, the last nail in the bull’s coffin was put when the lagging line broke below the Ichimoku cloud pattern. This indicates to investors that the fall will be swift and sharp, which is exactly what happened. Thus, the overall signs of a fall were there and I believe investors who followed technical analysis rules would have been rewarded substantially, as it would have resulted in them exiting long positions and entering short positions.
Daily chart:
The stock’s daily chart indicates to investors that they can go long on Apple in the long run. However, it still isn’t yet time for investors to make an entry as I expect a further correction. I say this due to the formation of a ‘Bearish Counterattack’ candle pattern. This candle pattern psychology indicates to investors that the bears currently have the upper hand. Moreover, the candle received further bearish confirmation as it formed at the lower falling window's resistance line. Thus, this signals to investors to wait for a few sessions before making an entry into the stock as it can be bought at a lower price.
On the price target front, I do not expect the stock to extend its fall beyond the 161.8% Fibonacci support level at $172.46. This is due to this level being a long-term candle support zone that was formed by a prior rising window. Moreover, once it corrects till this mark, I expect the equity to have a rally up till the 127.2% and 161.8% Fibonacci resistance levels. The 127.2% Fibonacci resistance level is at $183.47, whilst the 161.8% Fibonacci resistance level is at $186.71.
Weekly chart:
The stock’s weekly chart indicates that the bearish correction is about to end. I say this due to the formation of a ‘Bullish Counterattack’ candle pattern. This pattern psychology indicates to traders that the decline is exhausting itself. Moreover, the candle has taken support from the 100-day moving average, which solidifies my stance that a bullish reversal is round the corner. Furthermore, the stock has broken out from the bottom end of the Bollinger band, which indicates that the decline is exhausting itself. Lastly, the stock’s lagging line has turned upwards and is trading above the Ichimoku cloud which shows that a bullish reversal is highly likely.
On the price target front, I expect the stock to rise till the 100% to 127.2% Fibonacci resistance levels. The 100% Fibonacci resistance level is at $200.02, while the 127.2% Fibonacci resistance level is at $207.81. Once the equity does reach these levels, then I expect a sideways pattern to form.
On the indicator facet, the long-term RSI has commenced an ascent which depicts that the bulls are making a comeback. Furthermore, the ADX settings have perched between 30 and 34, thus, demonstrating to investors that there is an ongoing build-up in bullish pressure. Lastly, the accumulation and distribution rating has flattened out after being in decline for the prior three weeks. This shows that there is a change occurring in the balance between the bulls and bears, in which the bulls are slowly gaining an upper hand.
The big picture: Overall, Apple has undertaken various activities that will aid the firm in having a robust growth in its share price down the road. Thus, I am confident that the equity will soon be in a sweet spot where the probability of a long-term price rise is high. However, before trading, ensure that you utilize a trailing stop loss so that you are around for the next trade as capital protection is key.
Good luck trading.
